chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He should witness two men when he divorces and when he takes her back. If he was unaware, then he had intercourse with her, he should witness now regarding what he has done, and she is his wife. And if he did not witness when he divorced, then his divorce is not valid.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid divorce and remarriage according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of 'Talaq al-Sarih' (clear divorce) requiring two just witnesses for validity, a cornerstone of Shia fiqh distinguishing it from some Sunni schools. It highlights the legal consequence of failing to witness the divorce: if the husband consummates the marriage without prior witnessed divorce, the initial divorce is deemed null, and he must now produce witnesses to validate the remarriage, effectively treating the union as continuous.
